title: Closure of K-flat complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Bounded-above complexes of flat $\mathcal O$-modules [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] are K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex]. The class of K-flat complexes is closed under cones and countable direct sums (and hence under homotopy colimits), and countable direct sums of flat $\mathcal O$-modules are flat.

source.place: Lemma 06YS (K-flatness of bounded-above flat complexes and closure under the homotopy-colimit construction)

proof.text: Apply CochainComplex.isKFlat_of_boundedAbove_flat to the supplied upper bound and degreewise flatness hypotheses.
For a morphism of K-flat complexes apply CochainComplex.isKFlat_mappingCone.

Obtain the Grothendieck abelian property from grothendieckAbelian_with_localized_generator, and monoidal closure from tensorClosed. For any family of acyclic complexes, form in each degree the short complex of diagrams via ShortComplex.functorEquivalence. Evaluations jointly reflect isomorphisms and are exact, so the short complex of diagrams is exact. Apply Mathlib colim.exact_mapShortComplex to the termwise coproduct cocones: AB4 from the Grothendieck property makes the coproduct acyclic. Given an acyclic test complex A, the total-tensor functor in the other complex variable preserves coproducts by the source-library BifunctorColimits instance, since each tensor functor is left adjoint. Each tensor summand is acyclic by the given K-flatness. Transport acyclicity across preservesColimitIso and Discrete.compNatIsoDiscrete. This proves K-flatness of arbitrary u-small coproducts, in particular all countable ones. For index types in a separate universe that are Small.{u}, transport exactness from Discrete (Shrink.{u} I) along Discrete.equivalence (equivShrink I), using HasExactColimitsOfShape.of_domain_equivalence. The fully proved private helper isKFlat_coproduct_small therefore applies both to I : Type u and to the natural numbers without identifying universes.

Apply the preceding coproduct proof to the natural-number-indexed family. The endomorphism 1 - shift has that K-flat sum as both domain and codomain, so isKFlat_mappingCone proves K-flatness of its cone. The statement already writes the homotopy colimit as this cone, so no comparison to the ordinary colimit is needed.

Use the Grothendieck abelian property and monoidal closure as above. For each flat sheaf F_i, its tensorRight is exact by definition. BraidedCategory.tensorLeftIsoTensorRight transports its finite-limit preservation to tensorLeft; closure gives finite-colimit preservation of tensorLeft automatically. Thus F_i satisfies CategoryTheory.ObjectProperty.flat. Apply ObjectProperty.flat_coproduct and take its tensorRight exactness clause, which is definitionally SheafOfModules.IsFlat of the sum.

lean.statement: theorem kFlat_closure {C : Type u} [Category.{u} C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C} [J.WEqualsLocallyBijective AddCommGrpCat.{u}] [HasWeakSheafify J AddCommGrpCat.{u}] (R : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u}) : (∀ K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ, (∃ b : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, b < i → IsZero (K.X i)) → (∀ i : ℤ, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (K.X i)) → K.IsKFlat) ∧ (∀ (K L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (f : K ⟶ L), K.IsKFlat → L.IsKFlat → (mappingCone f).IsKFlat) ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) [Countable I], ∀ K : I → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ, (∀ i : I, (K i).IsKFlat) → (∐ K).IsKFlat) ∧ (∀ (K : ℕ → CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R)) ℤ) (t : ∀ n : ℕ, K n ⟶ K (n + 1)), (∀ n : ℕ, (K n).IsKFlat) → (mappingCone (𝟙 (∐ K) - Sigma.desc (fun n : ℕ => t n ≫ Sigma.ι K (n + 1)))).IsKFlat) ∧ (∀ (I : Type u) [Countable I], ∀ F : I → SheafOfModules.{u} ((sheafCompose J (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R), (∀ i : I, SheafOfModules.IsFlat (F i)) → SheafOfModules.IsFlat (∐ F))
